title: Ocean View Homes in Crescent Beach & Ocean Park | Jared Gibbons
description: Ocean view homes for sale in Crescent Beach and Ocean Park, South Surrey: live MLS® listings, what the area has sold for, and how to check a view.
h1: Ocean View Homes for Sale in Crescent Beach & Ocean Park
intro: This search shows Crescent Beach and Ocean Park homes with an ocean view, live from the MLS®. Below it are the sold prices for the area and what to check before you trust a view from a photo.
h_place: Where the water is in Crescent Beach and Ocean Park
place: Crescent Beach and Ocean Park are two different settings in one board sub-area. Crescent Beach is the low beachside village beside Boundary Bay and Mud Bay, across the water from Delta. Ocean Park sits up on the bluffs above the same shoreline.
The geography below is from public sources, so you can place a listing before you visit.
facts: Blackie Spit is the northern tip of Crescent Beach, beside Mud Bay near the Nicomekl River. Surrey created Blackie Spit Park there in 1996, and its shoreline is eelgrass, mudflat and tidal marsh, so the outlook changes with the tide (Wikipedia, Crescent Beach).
The shoreline from Crescent Rock, near 24 Avenue, to White Rock runs about 6.5 km at the base of the Ocean Park bluffs (Wikipedia, Crescent Beach).
Kwomais Point Park, at 1367 128 Street, is a bluff-top park with a viewing platform, a useful way to see what the bluff outlook is like before booking a showing.
BNSF Railway tracks cross both road accesses to Crescent Beach, Crescent Road and McBride Avenue (Wikipedia, Crescent Beach).
h_sold: What Crescent Beach and Ocean Park homes have sold for
sold_intro: These are closed sales for the board sub-area that holds both neighbourhoods, with the nearby sub-areas beside it for comparison.
table_caption: Crescent Beach and Ocean Park, with nearby areas: what sold
sold_caveat: These figures cover every home sold in each area, not only those with a view, because the closed-sales export does not separate them. Use the area median as the baseline. When a listing's price sits well above it, ask for recent sales on the same street with a similar outlook to see whether the view explains the gap.
h_check: Checking an ocean view before you make an offer
check_intro: A view in a listing is the agent's description and a photo taken from the best window. These are the checks that matter most here.
checks: Stand in the rooms where you will spend your time, and ask for a second visit at a different state of the tide, since the shore here includes mudflat and tidal marsh.
Ask what the lots between the home and the water may become under their zoning. A view is not guaranteed by title unless a covenant or view easement says so.
On an Ocean Park bluff lot, ask the City of Surrey whether a development permit area applies to the lot. The listing will not say.
In Crescent Beach, visit at a time when trains pass, and note where the home sits against the tracks and the two crossings.

faq.q: Does an ocean view always mean waterfront?
faq.a: No. Waterfront means the property touches the water. An ocean-view home looks out over it, often from a bluff or an upper floor, and sits on a separate lot. The waterfront searches are listed at the bottom of this page.

faq.q: Is the MLS® view field reliable?
faq.a: It is the listing agent's description, so treat it as a lead to confirm in person, not a measurement.

title: Ocean View Homes in Tsawwassen | Jared Gibbons
description: Ocean view homes for sale in Tsawwassen, Delta: live MLS® listings, sold prices by Tsawwassen sub-area, and the bluff and foreshore checks to make.
h1: Ocean View Homes for Sale in Tsawwassen
intro: This search shows Tsawwassen homes with an ocean view, live from the MLS®. Tsawwassen has two very different kinds of water view, from the bluff in the west and along Boundary Bay, and the sold prices below are split by sub-area so you can see which is which.
h_place: Bluff, beach and inland: where Tsawwassen views come from
place: Tsawwassen is the beachside part of Delta, next to the border and the BC Ferries terminal. The Paragon sub-areas give a rough map of where water views may be found: English Bluff and Cliff Drive on the higher ground in the west, Beach Grove and Boundary Beach along Boundary Bay, and Pebble Hill, Tsawwassen Central and the north and east sub-areas further inland.
Delta's Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), draws two hazard permit areas that matter most to view buyers, and both are mapped parcel by parcel.
facts: Hazard Development Permit Area SD2, English Bluff (the Tsawwassen Escarpment), covers the sloped lands on the western side. A geotechnical study can be required for a lot inside it.

Hazard Development Permit Area SD3 covers the Boundary Bay foreshore and the Southlands. It sets a minimum floor level of 2.9 m GSC datum for habitable space, a minimum ground level of 2.3 m around construction, and no building within 7.5 m of the natural boundary of a tidal area.
Whether a given lot sits in SD2 or SD3 can only be read from the City's DeltaMap for that parcel. The listing will not say.
Cliff Drive is a Paragon sub-area name, not an official City neighbourhood, and the escarpment area lies immediately to its west.
h_sold: What Tsawwassen homes have sold for, by sub-area
sold_intro: These closed sales cover every home in each sub-area, with no filter for view.
sold_caveat: Because the export has no view field, a bluff or beach sub-area median is a baseline for the sub-area, not a price for a view home. To see what a view added, ask for recent sales within a few streets of the home you like.
h_check: What to check on a Tsawwassen view home
check_intro: Water views here are tied to slope and shoreline, which is also where the permit areas sit, so the checks go together.
checks: Look the lot up on DeltaMap and note whether SD2 or SD3 applies, then ask what a geotechnical report or minimum floor level would mean for any renovation.
For Beach Grove and Boundary Beach lots, ask about flood protection and construction levels, since the foreshore rules apply to new building and some alterations.
On the bluff, look at what lies below the lot. Trees and neighbouring houses can change a view over the years.
A buyer's home inspection will not tell you whether the view is protected. Ask what the lots in front may build.

faq.q: Where in Tsawwassen are the ocean views?
faq.a: Mostly on the higher ground in English Bluff and Cliff Drive and along Boundary Bay in Beach Grove and Boundary Beach. The search above shows current listings flagged with an ocean view.

faq.q: How do I know if a Tsawwassen lot is in a hazard permit area?
faq.a: Look the parcel up on the City of Delta's DeltaMap. Hazard Development Permit Areas SD2 (English Bluff) and SD3 (Boundary Bay foreshore and the Southlands) are mapped there.

title: Mountain View Homes on Burke Mountain, Coquitlam | Jared Gibbons
description: Mountain view homes for sale on Burke Mountain, Coquitlam: live MLS® listings, what Burke Mountain and nearby upland areas sold for, and what to check.
h1: Mountain View Homes for Sale on Burke Mountain
intro: This search shows Burke Mountain homes with a mountain view, live from the MLS®. Burke Mountain is a growing hillside neighbourhood in northeast Coquitlam, so the checks on this page are as much about what is still being built as about what you can see.
h_place: Burke Mountain and the mountain behind it
place: Mount Burke itself is in northeast Coquitlam, and most of it lies inside Pinecone Burke Provincial Park, created in 1995 (Wikipedia, Mount Burke). The neighbourhood called Burke Mountain is the developed land on the lower southern slopes, and the City of Coquitlam has been planning it in stages.
That means a mountain view here is usually a view up to the park forest or across to other ridges, and it is tied to how much of the surrounding slope has been built.
facts: The City of Coquitlam's Northwest Burke Vision page sets out the planning for the northwest part of Burke Mountain.
Pinecone Burke Provincial Park protects most of the mountain itself, so the forest above the neighbourhood is mostly inside a protected park.
Burke Mountain is still building out, so parcels beside or below a home may be vacant, under construction or approved for development.
h_sold: What Burke Mountain and nearby upland areas have sold for
sold_intro: These closed sales cover every home in each area, with no filter for view. The neighbouring upland sub-areas are included for comparison.
table_caption: Burke Mountain and nearby upland Coquitlam areas: what sold
sold_caveat: These figures include townhomes and houses of every outlook. The closed-sales export has no view field, so compare a listing with sales on the same street and at the same elevation rather than only with the area median.
h_check: What to check on a Burke Mountain view home
check_intro: The view is only as permanent as the land in front of it, so the first questions are about the neighbouring parcels.
checks: Ask the City of Coquitlam what is approved or planned for the parcels in front of and below the home.
On a sloped lot, check the retaining walls, drainage and who owns them, and read the strata minutes if the home is a townhome.
Visit on a clear day and again when the cloud is low. Hillside views are often partly in cloud.
Ask whether the view looks at the park forest, other homes or the valley, since that decides how stable it is.

faq.q: Is Burke Mountain still being built?
faq.a: Yes. The City of Coquitlam is planning and approving development in stages, so parcels near a home may be vacant or under construction. Ask the City what is planned beside any home you like.

faq.q: Do all Burke Mountain homes have mountain views?
faq.a: No. A view depends on the lot's elevation and what stands in front of it, and the MLS® view field is the listing agent's description.

title: Mountain View Homes in Maple Ridge | Jared Gibbons
description: Mountain view homes for sale in Maple Ridge: live MLS® listings, sold prices for Silver Valley, Albion, Thornhill and other upland areas, and what to check.
h1: Mountain View Homes for Sale in Maple Ridge
intro: This search shows Maple Ridge homes with a mountain view, live from the MLS®. Maple Ridge sits against the mountains on its north side, so a lot of the district has some outlook. The sold prices below help you see where that outlook costs more.
h_place: Where Maple Ridge meets the mountains
place: The District of Maple Ridge names ten neighbourhoods on its website: Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster's Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon. The ones that matter most for mountain views are on the north and east sides.
facts: Silver Valley lies north of the Alouette River, and the District describes it as having views and trail networks.
Whonnock is a lakeside recreation area on the east side, with mountains rising in the background of the District's own photograph.
Yennadon lists Golden Ears Provincial Park among its attractions.
Thornhill is described by the District as heavily forested and mainly residential, with some farms and nurseries.
h_sold: What Maple Ridge homes have sold for, by area
sold_intro: These closed sales cover every home in each sub-area, with no filter for view. They are the baseline a view home is priced against.
sold_caveat: The closed-sales data has no view field, so these medians describe each area as a whole. Use them as the baseline and compare a listing with sales on its own street.
h_check: What to check on a Maple Ridge mountain view
check_intro: Hillside and rural parts of Maple Ridge bring a few practical checks that a photo will not show.
checks: Confirm the zoning of the parcels in front of the home, since a subdivision can change a view.
On rural and upland lots, ask about water supply, septic and snow, and whether the road is District-maintained.
Look at the view in winter as well as summer, when leaves are down and cloud is lower.
In Whonnock and Thornhill, ask about the Agricultural Land Reserve status of the land beside the home.

faq.q: Which Maple Ridge neighbourhoods have mountain views?
faq.a: The District points to views in Silver Valley, and mountains show behind Whonnock. The search above shows listings currently flagged with a mountain view.

faq.a: It can, but the closed-sales data has no view field, so the sold table shows each area as a whole. Ask for comparable sales on the same street.

title: Mountain View Homes in Chilliwack | Jared Gibbons
description: Mountain view homes for sale in Chilliwack: live MLS® listings, sold prices for Eastern Hillsides, Promontory and Chilliwack Mountain, and what to check.
h1: Mountain View Homes for Sale in Chilliwack
intro: This search shows Chilliwack homes with a mountain view, live from the MLS®. Chilliwack is built on flat farmland with mountains on three sides, and the hillside neighbourhoods are where the outlook is widest.
h_place: The hillsides and valleys around Chilliwack
place: Chilliwack's flat valley floor is ringed by mountains, and homes on the rising ground at the edge of town are the ones that look across it. In board terms those are sub-areas such as Eastern Hillsides, Promontory, Chilliwack Mountain and Little Mountain.
facts: Yarrow sits between Vedder Mountain to the south and Sumas Mountain to the northwest, at the foot of the Skagit Range (Wikipedia, Neighbourhoods in Chilliwack).
Greendale lies at the base of Sumas Mountain, on the bed of the drained Sumas Lake.
Ryder Lake is a small sub-alpine farming community on Mount Thom.
The Chilliwack River Valley runs 47 km and is known for hiking and outdoor recreation.
h_sold: What Chilliwack hillside homes have sold for
sold_intro: These closed sales cover every home in each sub-area, with no filter for view.
sold_caveat: The export has no view field, so a hillside sub-area median is a baseline for that sub-area. A view home on the same hill is likely priced above it, and how far above is best checked against recent sales on its own street.
h_check: What to check on a Chilliwack hillside view
check_intro: Hillsides bring their own checks. The first two matter on almost every listing.
checks: Ask about slope stability, drainage and retaining walls on any sloped lot, and read the geotechnical report if there is one.
Look at what could be built in front of the home under its zoning, and whether any of it is in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
On upland and rural lots, ask about water and septic, winter road access and snow clearing.
Visit on a clear morning and in rain. Mountain views on this side of the valley change a great deal with the weather.

faq.q: Which Chilliwack areas have mountain views?
faq.a: The hillside sub-areas, such as Eastern Hillsides, Promontory, Chilliwack Mountain and Little Mountain, are the likeliest. The search above shows listings currently flagged with a mountain view.

faq.q: How reliable is the view field on a listing?
faq.a: It is the listing agent's description, so confirm the view in person, in more than one kind of weather.

title: Mountain View Homes in Abbotsford | Jared Gibbons
description: Mountain view homes for sale in Abbotsford: live MLS® listings, sold prices for Sumas Mountain and Abbotsford East and West, and what to check on a view.
h1: Mountain View Homes for Sale in Abbotsford
intro: This search shows Abbotsford homes with a mountain view, live from the MLS®. Abbotsford has a mountain in the middle of its eastern side, Sumas Mountain, and a flat prairie to its south, so the outlook depends heavily on which side of that line a home is on.
h_place: Sumas Mountain and the land around it
place: Sumas Mountain lies between Abbotsford and Chilliwack, on the south bank of the Fraser River. Urban Abbotsford is to its west, and the historic community of Straiton is in the central part of the mountain. The board's Sumas Mountain sub-area is on the mountain itself, and Abbotsford East and West are listed beside it in the table below.
facts: Sumas Mountain Provincial Park covers the northern part of the mountain, and the eastern reaches are mostly wilderness overlooking Greendale in Chilliwack.
Farming, gravel mining and logging continue on parts of the mountain, and brick-clay mining once gave rise to Clayburn.
Sumas Prairie to the south is the bed of the drained Sumas Lake and forms part of the Fraser River floodplain.
The mountain shields McDonald Park, a dark-sky preserve, from city light.
h_sold: What Abbotsford homes have sold for near the mountain
sold_intro: These closed sales cover every home in each sub-area, with no filter for view.
table_caption: Abbotsford sub-areas near Sumas Mountain: what sold
sold_caveat: The closed-sales export has no view field, so these medians describe each sub-area as a whole. A mountain-view home is best priced against recent sales close by with a similar outlook.
h_check: What to check on an Abbotsford mountain view
check_intro: The mountain itself is working land as well as scenery, which shapes what to check.
checks: On Sumas Mountain, ask about nearby gravel, logging or farming activity and how it affects noise and truck traffic.
For Sumas Prairie homes, ask for flood history and floodplain information, since the land is the former lake bed.
Check the water supply and septic arrangement on rural and mountain lots, and ask who maintains the road.
Look at the view at different times of day and in different weather before you decide how much it is worth.

faq.q: Where are the mountain views in Abbotsford?
faq.a: On and around Sumas Mountain, and on the higher ground in Abbotsford East and West. The search above shows listings currently flagged with a mountain view.

faq.q: Is Sumas Prairie a flood risk?
faq.a: Sumas Prairie is the bed of the drained Sumas Lake and part of the Fraser River floodplain, so ask for flood and drainage information on any home there.
